questionText:
Consider an array $A$ of integers of size $n$. The indices of $A$ run from $1$ to $n$. An algorithm is to be designed to check whether $A$ satisfies the condition given below.

$$\forall i, j \in \{1, \dots, n - 1\} \text{ such that } i > j, (A[i + 1] - A[i]) > (A[j + 1] - A[j])$$

Which one of the following gives the worst case time complexity of the fastest algorithm that can be designed for the problem?
explanation:
Step-by-step Explanation:

1. Understand the Condition:
Let $D[k] = A[k + 1] - A[k]$ represent the difference between adjacent elements for $k \in \{1, 2, \dots, n - 1\}$.
The condition states that for all $i > j$, $D[i] > D[j]$. This means the sequence of differences $D[1], D[2], \dots, D[n - 1]$ must be strictly increasing.

2. Checking Increasing Order:
To check if a sequence of length $n - 1$ is strictly increasing, we only need to verify if $D[k] > D[k - 1]$ for all $k$ from $2$ to $n - 1$.
This requires comparing adjacent differences, which can be done in a single linear pass of time $O(n)$.

3. Lower Bound:
Since any deterministic algorithm must read the elements of array $A$ of size $n$ to verify the condition in the worst case, the time lower bound is $\Omega(n)$.

Combining the upper and lower bounds, the worst-case time complexity of the fastest algorithm is $\Theta(n)$.
